issues.legal_issue: A litigant seeking equitable writ relief cannot rely on a materially false assertion that no personal hearing was provided.
material_facts: The foundation asserted that its objections to the acquisition had been rejected without a personal hearing.
The record showed that the foundation was represented by counsel at the hearing, was given an opportunity to be heard, and was offered the opportunity to file fresh objections.
The foundation gave no satisfactory explanation for its assertion that no hearing had occurred.
issues.conclusion: The assertion that no personal hearing had been given was baseless and factually incorrect, and the foundation’s conduct was reprehensible; a person invoking the court’s equitable extraordinary jurisdiction must come with clean hands and must not conceal material facts.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising its equitable extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, a court requires the applicant to come with clean hands and not conceal material facts. The Court referred to Farid Ahmed Abdul Samad v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad & Anr., [1977] 1 SCR 71.

rule.if: extraordinary_writ_proceeding and no_hearing_claim_made and hearing_was_provided and material_hearing_facts_not_satisfactorily_explained

predicates.extraordinary_writ_proceeding: The party sought extraordinary writ relief from a court.
predicates.no_hearing_claim_made: The party claimed that it had not been given a personal hearing.
predicates.hearing_was_provided: The party was in fact represented and given an opportunity to be heard.
predicates.material_hearing_facts_not_satisfactoril: The party did not satisfactorily explain the record showing that a hearing had been provided.

issues.definition: When a party seeking extraordinary writ relief claims that it received no hearing despite having been heard, and does not satisfactorily explain the contrary record, the claim is rejected as false.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to acquisition proceedings brought after substantial unexplained delay may be rejected for laches when the grounds were available earlier.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was issued in 1959, and the declarations covering the land were issued in 1968 and 1969, but the foundation did not challenge them until 1973.
The grounds later advanced against the earlier notifications were available when those notifications were issued.
The foundation withdrew its first writ petition and later filed another on substantially the same grounds, without identifying a fresh circumstance that justified the later filing.
The later notices concerned only a small portion of the land, while the challenge concerned notifications covering the whole area.
The absence of an award and the fact that the foundation remained in possession did not explain the delay; the foundation had itself sought a stay against making the award and dispossessing it.
The Court relied on Aflatoon & Ors. v. Lt. Governor Delhi & Ors., [1975] 1 SCR 802, which applied laches to a delayed challenge to land-acquisition proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the acquisition notifications was liable to be dismissed for laches and delay. The appeal was dismissed with costs, and the Court found it unnecessary to decide the other questions of law raised.
issues.legal_principle: A writ challenge under Article 226 may be rejected for laches where the grounds for challenging acquisition notifications were available when they were issued but the challenger waited without adequate explanation. Later notices relating to only part of the land, continued possession, and the absence of an award do not by themselves justify delay in challenging earlier notifications. The Court applied Aflatoon & Ors. v. Lt. Governor Delhi & Ors., [1975] 1 SCR 802, concerning notifications and declarations under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

rule.if: writ_challenge_to_acquisition_proceedings and challenge_grounds_available_earlier and substantial_delay and no_adequate_explanation_for_delay

predicates.writ_challenge_to_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding is a writ challenge to land-acquisition proceedings.
predicates.challenge_grounds_available_earlier: The grounds relied on to challenge the acquisition were available when the challenged notifications were issued.
predicates.substantial_delay: The challenger waited a substantial period before raising those grounds in court.
predicates.no_adequate_explanation_for_delay: The challenger offered no adequate explanation for waiting, and the circumstances relied on did not justify the delay.

issues.definition: A writ challenge to acquisition proceedings is rejected for laches when its grounds were available earlier, the challenger waited substantially, and the delay is not adequately explained.
